random_sample_judgment.title: Scope Classification Workshop
random_sample_judgment.context: Analyze rules students use to classify classroom examples as microeconomics or macroeconomics. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Unit-level study covers one buyer or one seller, whereas economy-wide study covers national totals.
Economy-wide consumer price inflation published monthly is macroeconomics.
The discipline develops models at both unit level and aggregate level to handle scarcity.
All government activity is automatically macroeconomics.
Canteen meals are macro because food affects national health spending.
random_sample_judgment.note: Statements use core micro/business-economics vocabulary consistent with school texts.

random_sample_judgment.title: Barter weekend market
random_sample_judgment.context: A hobby market allows only direct swaps: honey for bread, bread for pottery. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Barter requires double coincidence of wants between each pair of traders.
Absence of money as medium of exchange makes multilateral trading chains harder to arrange.
Such swaps still constitute exchange under otherwise unchanged conditions.
Barter eliminates all comparison problems because traders always value goods equally.
Introducing money would add medium of exchange simplifying trades that barter complicates.
random_sample_judgment.note: Statements use core micro/business-economics vocabulary consistent with school texts.

random_sample_judgment.title: Market Variants Final Synthesis
random_sample_judgment.context: Analyze free, social, and eco-social market economies relative to planned coordination and post-planned transformation. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Market versus planned distinguishes price coordination from central directive coordination economy-wide.
Free market economy stresses private ownership, profit incentives, and consumer sovereignty.
Social market economy adds welfare and social partnership while keeping competitive product markets.
Eco-social models extend social market design by embedding ecological sustainability alongside competitive markets.
Transformation from planned systems shifts toward privatisation, competition, and price liberalisation over time.
random_sample_judgment.note: Statements use core micro/business-economics vocabulary consistent with school texts.

random_sample_judgment.title: German social partners
random_sample_judgment.context: Employers' associations negotiate with unions under legal framework while firms compete in product markets. Evaluate social market:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Eco-social market systems abolish prices and reinstate pure planning for green goals.
Co-determination and welfare institutions aim at social peace without abolishing private firms.
Social market means unions set all output quotas replacing consumer demand entirely.
Market competition among firms can coexist with worker representation rules.
Eco-social market would add stronger environmental standards to this social-market base.
random_sample_judgment.note: Statements use core micro/business-economics vocabulary consistent with school texts.

random_sample_judgment.title: Consumer boycott effect
random_sample_judgment.context: Shoppers boycott a brand over labour practices; sales collapse and retailer delists it. Evaluate market economy mechanisms:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Consumer spending choices can punish firms that lose public trust, illustrating consumer sovereignty.
Boycotts prove planned economies operate in every retail sector because only planners can delist goods.
Profit motive leads retailers to respond when falling demand threatens revenue.
Market prices and sales volumes signal reputational damage faster than quota revisions would.
Social market economy still relies on consumer demand signals alongside labour regulation.
random_sample_judgment.note: Statements use core micro/business-economics vocabulary consistent with school texts.

random_sample_judgment.title: Capstone Scenarios in Market Analysis
random_sample_judgment.context: Review applied combinations of demand shifts, supply shifts, and inflation policy in everyday economic settings. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Raising interest rates to fight inflation may slow housing demand by increasing mortgage costs.
Too much money relative to output can raise general prices even when one industry's supply expands.
A café facing higher coffee bean costs and rising commuter demand may see ambiguous price change.
Markets coordinate plans through prices, while policy may alter incentives via taxes, subsidies, or rates.
When festival demand surges but venue capacity is fixed, equilibrium ticket price tends to fall.
random_sample_judgment.note: Statements use core micro/business-economics vocabulary consistent with school texts.

random_sample_judgment.title: Plant Capacity Expansion
random_sample_judgment.context: Consider a manufacturing plant adding a production line that raises monthly output without raising unit prices. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: If demand stays fixed while supply shifts right, equilibrium price may fall.
At the new equilibrium, quantity traded may exceed the old equilibrium if demand is unchanged.
Higher raw-material input prices could partially offset the expansion by shifting supply leftward.
Customers ordering the product face lower shortage risk after a successful supply expansion.
Adding capacity that lowers unit cost can shift supply rightward for the manufactured good.
random_sample_judgment.note: Statements use core micro/business-economics vocabulary consistent with school texts.

random_sample_judgment.title: Systems Models Closing Review
random_sample_judgment.context: Analyze market versus planned coordination together with free, social, and eco-social market variants. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Planned economies coordinate through central targets; market economies coordinate through prices and private incentives.
Free market economy highlights private property, competition, and consumer sovereignty.
Social market economy adds welfare and social partnership without eliminating competitive product markets.
Eco-social market economy integrates environmental sustainability with social market foundations.
Transformation from planned toward market systems includes privatisation and price liberalisation reforms.
random_sample_judgment.note: Statements use core micro/business-economics vocabulary consistent with school texts.

random_sample_judgment.title: A small IT-support venture Factor Bundle
random_sample_judgment.context: Analyze the factor bundle in a laptop repair and software venture. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Hands-on technical fault-finding by staff is counted as the labour factor among the firm's resources.
Licensed diagnostic software and repair tools represent technology in the service model.
Refurbishing laptops uses spare parts inventory as capital.
The venture relies on entrepreneurship alone with no other factors.
Customer contact replaces all other factors in the venture.
random_sample_judgment.note: Statements use core micro/business-economics vocabulary consistent with school texts.

random_sample_judgment.title: Profit versus environment conflict
random_sample_judgment.context: Consider higher profit targets may clash with environmental spending. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Higher profit targets may clash with environmental spending on cleaner production.
Profit and environmental protection align perfectly with no trade-offs in every decision.
Owners and environmental stakeholders agree on every spending priority without exception.
Pollution control investments raise costs but create no tension with owner stakeholder interests.
Cleaner production spending can lower short-term profit and tension owner and environmental aims.
random_sample_judgment.note: Statements use core micro/business-economics vocabulary consistent with school texts.

random_sample_judgment.context: Review linking GDP per capita to living standards. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Living standards correlate with GDP though GDP misses some welfare dimensions.
Per capita averages miss distribution of income within a country.
GDP per capita fully captures inequality within a country.
Higher GDP per capita in EU members is unrelated to living standards.
Low GDP per capita alone defines an emerging economy's entire sector mix.
random_sample_judgment.note: Statements use core micro/business-economics vocabulary consistent with school texts.

random_sample_judgment.title: GDP Income Coverage Critique
random_sample_judgment.context: Review criticisms that GDP misses some income. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: GDP omission of some income sources is one reason its use is debated.
Every barter transaction is always fully recorded in official GDP.
Unpaid home maintenance done by owners is always included in GDP.
GDP fully captures household volunteering and unpaid care in its totals.
Household volunteering and unpaid care are always counted in official GDP totals.

random_sample_judgment.context: Analyze a firm imports finished goods for domestic resale without foreign production. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A firm that manufactures abroad but sells only at home still crosses into international scope.
Undercapitalisation is solved once a regional firm wins one large nearby contract.
Geographic scope labels depend on where a firm operates and sells, not owner residence alone.

Domestic public tenders make a firm multinational by exposing it to government rules.

Apprentices cutting patterns and stitching garments supply labour.
Tailoring needs only labour because designs exist in the tailor's head.
Machines on hire-purchase are land because they occupy workshop space.

random_sample_judgment.context: Analyze whether leased assets count as capital. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
